Q: Fill a column with check boxes till the last row of the data A:

Fill the column with checkboxes and hide the ones you don't want to show by using a conditional formatting custom formula rule that sets text color to white when there are no values in the preceding row, like this:

=counta(A2:F2) = 0

...where F signifies the last column you want to test.

I don't think this request really fits an "open-ended question" category such as Advice. This is really more of a troubleshooting question.

Q: Visual artifacts when exporting pie charts via ggplot ggsave A:

The following worked, R version 4.5.3 (2026-03-11 ucrt) on Windows 11.

png(filename = str_c("pie", ".png"),
    width = 8.5,
    height = 7.64,
    units = "in",
    res = 300L
)
pie
dev.off()

From the documentation, help("ggsave"), my emphasis.

device
Device to use. Can either be a device function (e.g. png), or one of "eps", "ps", "tex" (pictex), "pdf", "jpeg", "tiff", "png", "bmp", "svg" or "wmf" (windows only). If NULL (default), the device is guessed based on the filename extension.

Don't let ggsave guess the device based on the file extension, use the device png() explicitly and the artifact is gone.

ggsave(filename = str_c("pie", ".png"),
       plot = pie,
       path = "outputs",
       width = 8.5,
       height = NA,
       units = "in",
       dpi = 300,
       device = png
       )

Q: How to separate runtime dependencies from development dependencies? A:

Using pip and poetry to install packages is not the same thing. And since you are using poetry as your python package manager, I recommend you stick to it.

Regarding your need for separation of development and testing dependency group, poetry already allows such grouping which can be described in pyproject.toml which you can read about here.

But with groups, you will have to keep a very specific separation of the files and command which need to be run as entrypoint with each group so you don't run into an ImportError .

Q: Migrating from expo to React native crashes the app A:

React Native Core team at Meta are officially recommend to use Framework like Expo as default way to build RN apps.

Looking at your dependencies graph, There's no special native modules which force you to eject from Expo.

Instead create brand new RN project which is prone to errors and misconfigurations, use Expo CGN to generative /android and /ios and add your native code/configurations.

In 2026, There's no real incentive to eject form Expo.

If ejecting still favorable option, Use Adb Logcat from Android Studio to inspect what cause crash.
